tob-4282: Apollodorus’s Book-hoard — in Frazer’s Englishing — is the great handbook of Greek god-tales, summing gods and heroes from the wells. The 100s compiler saved tales else lost. Frazer’s notes fatten the text. The work is the classic one-book Greek wonder-tales.
cia-0000107982: A May 1977 weekly survey article on nuclear cooperation between Pakistan and China. Beijing's help — designs, materials, know-how — would prove decisive in Pakistan's drive for the bomb. The report shows the CIA spotting, in real time, a partnership that reshaped the nuclear map of Asia.
cia-0000108482: An untitled July 1981 cable on Guatemalan human rights issues — the archive's spelling says Guatenalan. Guatemala's security forces were killing civilians on a massive scale, and Washington debated how much to know and say. The cable is a fragment of that debate, flashed from the field.
cia-0000126882: An August 1968 report on the status of Warsaw Pact forces in Czechoslovakia. The invasion armies were settling into occupation — garrisons, patrols, and a sullen population. The document tracks the mechanics of occupation: how an empire digs in after the tanks stop rolling.
cia-0000126982: An October 1975 report on heavy Soviet press coverage of the USSR's Angola involvement. Moscow was no longer hiding its backing of the MPLA — the propaganda was the policy. The document reads the volume of coverage as a measure of commitment: the louder the press, the deeper the involvement.
cia-0000132282: Situation Report 591 with a special spot commentary: Saddam defiant and determined. The spot format marked this as essential reading — the enemy leader's mood, assessed. The document is psychological profiling at wartime tempo: defiance, measured.
cia-0000132382: Briefing material on Cuba with attached briefing material, dated June 1960 — the truncated title suggests layers of preparation. Briefing books were built like Russian dolls: summaries within summaries. The entry is the paperwork behind the policy: Cuba, thoroughly briefed.
cia-0000132482: Item three in the April 1960 series: new Cuban attacks on the United States — verbal, diplomatic, propagandistic. Havana's rhetoric was escalating with its revolution. The document catalogs the war of words: the insults, tallied.
cia-0000132582: Item 10 in the September 1960 series: Fidel Castro commenting on current Cuban policies. The leader's words were policy — speeches as decrees. The document is the voice, recorded: the maximum leader, explaining himself.
cia-0000136282: A 1954 cable from LINCOLN reporting urgency for delivery of planes on time. The aircraft were late; the operation could not wait. The document is the urgency: the planes, demanded — on schedule.
cia-0000136982: A 1954 cable on a message from a deleted person on distortion of Guatemalan developments — the archive's spelling says destortion. The narrative war. The entry is the complaint: the distortion, alleged — through a typo.
cia-0000138982: A 1946 military information report on Russian aid to Chinese communists — the companion to the Manchuria file. The assistance, tallied. The document is the ledger: the aid, itemized.
un-ga-res-a-69-82: General Assembly Resolution A/69/82, adopted in 2014 during the 69th session. The eighty-second act. The designation and year are certain; the decision is in the text.

un-sc-res-982: Security Council Resolution 982, adopted in 1995 — aligned. The deliberations continued. The number and year endure; the decision is in the text.
un-sc-res-1582: Security Council Resolution 1582, cataloged with the year 2001 — the numbering suggests 2005, a mismatch. The designation is kept; the date is doubted.
cia-0000132782: A 1960 CIA Cuban developments file — number 0000132782, the final entry of this shard. The 1960 Cuba run closes. The entry is the close: the shard, complete — the watch, preserved.
cia-0000139482: A 1988 CIA Project Sun Streak file, numbered 0000139482. The remote-viewing program's files multiplied. The entry is the multiplication: the folders, many.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d82: The Secretary of State to the President, October 31, 1943 — Document 82. The department's Halloween briefing. The memo is the briefing: the secretary, informing.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d182: The Secretary of State to the President, November 1, 1943 — Document 182. November's first briefing. The memo is the month's opening: the secretary, informing.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d282: A memorandum by the Generalissimo's chief of staff, Stilwell — the truncated title cuts off the date — Document 282. Vinegar Joe's paper. The memo is the general's: Stilwell, writing.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d382: The supervising Secret Service agent Reilly to the White House — the truncated title cuts off the rest — Document 382. The bodyguard's report. The memo is the protection: Reilly, reporting.
bat-wing-pg6382: Sax Rohmer, famed for the villainous Dr. Fu Manchu, turns to classic detective mystery in this thriller. A country-house murder with a seemingly impossible method draws investigators into a web of secrets and sinister atmosphere. Fans of early-twentieth-century crime fiction will find all the period pleasures here: fog, suspense, and a puzzle that keeps the pages turning.
arxiv-2605-08982: Giving a model more thinking time at inference improves answers, but the search must be principled and parallel. Yaniv Oren, Viliam Vadocz, Joery A. de Vries, and Wendelin Böhme propose PMCTS — particle Monte Carlo tree search — for scaling inference-time compute. The 2026 paper makes test-time thinking both rigorous and fast.
arxiv-2605-09482: Metriplectic systems blend Hamiltonian mechanics with dissipation — conserving energy while growing entropy at the same time. Philip J. Morrison and Yong-Geun Oh study them on contact manifolds, a natural geometric home. The 2026 paper is geometric mechanics on a rich stage.
arxiv-2605-09582: Singular product spaces — products marred by bad points — need both topology and category theory to be understood. Yusuke Hayashi and Tristan van der Vlugt bring both toolkits to bear on them. The 2026 paper is pure mathematics on beautifully rough spaces.
arxiv-2605-09682: When a Lambda-b baryon decays to Lambda plus D, spin and flavor entangle — and the pattern reveals weak phases. Yong Du, Chao-Qiang Geng, Xiao-Gang He, and colleagues extract them. The 2026 paper is flavor physics at its most delicate.
arxiv-2605-09782: Sinkhorn algorithms solve optimal transport problems fast; generalizing them to bounded-genus graphs in near-linear time is the real prize. Krzysztof Choromanski, Derek Long, Ananya Parashar, and colleagues claim exactly that. The 2026 paper is fast algorithms running at near-linear speed.
arxiv-2605-09882: Astronomical simulations need ray-tracing for three-dimensional direction-dependent equations — and it must be fast. Zhengping Zhu, Thomas G. Bisbas, Xuefei Tang, and colleagues build RAYTHEIA: a high-performance ray-tracing algorithm. The 2026 paper is computational astrophysics at speed.
plos-pone-0003382: A drug-repurposing lead emerged for a neglected fungal disease in this 2008 study. Fonsecaea pedrosoi causes chromoblastomycosis, a chronic skin infection with poor treatment options. The researchers showed that HIV peptidase inhibitors, drugs already used against AIDS, can arrest key fungal enzymes, suggesting existing medicines might be turned against this stubborn pathogen.
plos-pone-0003482: Virologists caught cytomegalovirus sabotaging the immune alarm in this 2008 paper. Plasmacytoid dendritic cells are the body's main producers of antiviral interferon, and the team showed human cytomegalovirus impairs them inside lymphoid organs. By muting the very cells that sound the alert, the virus buys itself cover, a classic move in the host-pathogen arms race.
plos-pone-0003582: Neuroanatomist Caio Maximino tested whether the fish brain's visual roof got simpler over time in this 2008 study. The tectum, the midbrain's visual processing hub, is often called evolutionarily conserved, but his cladistic analysis of non-tetrapods found real changes in complexity. The result complicates the story of a structure long assumed frozen.
plos-pone-0003682: In 2008, Andersson, Isaksson, and Wefer tested a DNA vaccine against a rat model of multiple sclerosis. The shot, encoding a myelin protein piece, dampened the harmful Th17 immune cells that drive the disease. The result shows DNA vaccination can retune a misfiring immune attack on the nervous system.
plos-pone-0003782: Blinder, Cove, and Foox found distant dendrites teaming up in this 2008 paper. Non-sister dendritic branches converged their activity to strengthen network connections, guided by the activity itself. The finding shows developing circuits reinforcing the paths they actually use.
plos-pone-0003882: Back in 2008, a group mapped the chromosomes of a lab butterfly. Bicyclus anynana, a workhorse of evolutionary study, got its first cytogenetic portrait plus an AFLP-based gene map. The chromosome and linkage data give geneticists the scaffolding this model insect had been missing.
plos-pone-0003982: In 2008, Jackson, Cummins, and Brady timed the brain flipping between views. Their reversible biological-motion figure sparked rapid switching between two rival perceptions. The team compared its reversal dynamics with those of classic ambiguous figures. The timing data reveal how the visual brain settles, then unsettles, what it sees.
plos-pone-0004082: In 2008, Eichorst, Lu, and Xu watched a molecular switch in moving cells. FRET biosensors tracked RhoA dynamics in migratory and stationary cells. Robot image analysis turned long movies into numbers. The new maps show where the switch fires during motion.
plos-pone-0004182: In 2009, Zhu, Sun, and Zhang tied a master switch to artery thickening. PGC-1alpha drove glucose-triggered growth and movement in artery wall cells. The key regulator links high blood sugar to atherosclerosis. Blocking it could slow vessel disease in diabetes patients.
plos-pone-0004282: In 2009, Wang and Burns found naloxone's hidden handshake. A pentapeptide site on filamin A blocked mu opioid receptor-Gs coupling. Ultra-low-dose naloxone stopped the excitatory switch cold. The site explains naloxone's odd boost effect. The finding refines opioid combination therapies greatly.
plos-pone-0352682: Children in the emergency department often get blood drawn twice — once at their clinic, once again at the hospital. This study modeled when repeat testing is truly necessary in pediatric EDs. Predicting necessity could spare kids painful re-draws and cut waste.
plos-pone-0349282: Killing staph on living skin without harming the patient is the trick. This study tested cold atmospheric plasma against Staphylococcus aureus colonies on living animal tissue surfaces. The effectiveness results probe whether plasma could become a practical wound-disinfection tool that spares healthy tissue.
plos-pone-0351782: As the climate shifts, freshwater species need connected refuges to survive. This paper designed a freshwater resilient and connected network to sustain biodiversity under a changing climate. The network blueprint shows conservationists which waters to link so that aquatic life can move as conditions change around it.
plos-pone-0343482: Dementia care planning should be personal — but primary care appointments are rushed. This study captured perceptions of personalised dementia care planning conversations: the time, the talk, and the teamwork involved. The findings show what good planning conversations actually need to work.
plos-pone-0357782: Odd sounds yank our attention away — but does repeating a response change how distracting they are? This study tested distraction by deviant sounds, comparing response repetition against response change. The findings reveal how the brain handles surprise differently when it is already acting versus when it must switch gears.
plos-pone-0356182: 3D-printing titanium parts demands precisely tuned laser power. This paper studied the effect of laser power variation on the microstructure and properties of selective laser melting coatings deposited on TC4 titanium alloy. The findings help engineers dial in the laser for stronger, more reliable printed parts.
plos-pone-0357382: Three-dimensional animation files are enormous — and streaming them demands smarter compression. This paper optimized 3D animation compression using structured processing and adaptive spatiotemporal segmentation. The algorithm shrinks animations dramatically without any visible loss of quality.
plos-pone-0357482: Blanket fertilizer application wastes money and pollutes waterways. Smart fertigation automates fertilizer delivery based on actual plant growth, using digital sensors with IoT capability. The system feeds each plant precisely what it needs, when it needs it — no more, no less.
plos-pone-0355282: When humanities undergraduates co-create with generative AI, what happens to their sense of agency? This paper studied GenAI-supported co-creation: offloading, agency, and future task confidence within a stimulus-organism-response framework. The findings map the emerging human-AI creative contract in education.
plos-pone-0337982: Lifetime data with censoring demands specialized statistics. This simulation-based study used an adaptive Type-II hybrid progressive censoring scheme to investigate the coefficient of variation of the weighted exponential distribution. The statistical advances sharpen reliability analysis for engineers.
plos-pone-0350782: Gonorrhea is outrunning antibiotics — and entirely new weapons are needed. This paper reported the pre-clinical efficacy of a C4BP hexameric IgG Fc fusion protein against Neisseria gonorrhoeae. The engineered protein recruits the immune system’s own machinery to kill the bacteria, showing potent activity in laboratory models and offering genuine hope against drug-resistant gonorrhea.
plos-pone-0353482: COPD doesn’t just damage the lungs — it disrupts the autonomic nervous system that governs the heart. This paper examined the relation between physical activity and cardiac autonomic dysfunction in COPD patients. The findings suggest that staying active may protect the heart’s neural control even as the lungs fail, adding urgency to pulmonary rehabilitation.
plos-pone-0353382: Europe’s pollinators need a common language for data to be shared. The EU pollinator hub controlled vocabulary is exactly that — an ontology for pollinators. This paper presented the structured vocabulary that lets researchers, farmers, and policymakers talk about bees, butterflies, and their kin without talking past each other.
plos-pone-0356782: Liver cirrhosis patients need sustained follow-up — and nurses may be the answer. This qualitative study explored aspects of implementing a nurse-based follow-up for these patients. The firsthand perspectives reveal what makes nurse-led cirrhosis care work in practice, not just on paper.
plos-pone-0356482: Virtual screening for drug candidates produces ranked lists — but decisions need calibrated confidence. TASC-VS moves from ranking to decision with calibration-aware top-k virtual screening. The method tells drug hunters not just which compounds rank highest, but which are actually worth synthesizing.
plos-pone-0356382: Radiomic features from diffusion-weighted MRI could diagnose pediatric brain tumors — but only if they’re stable. This paper evaluated how segmentation strategies affect radiomic feature stability. The findings tell radiologists which tumor-drawing methods yield trustworthy AI inputs for children’s cancer diagnosis.
plos-pone-0355682: Black cumin — Nigella sativa — is a valuable Ethiopian crop, but its yield stability was unmapped. This paper analyzed the stability of seed yield and agronomic performance across genotypes in the Amhara Region. The stability analysis identifies varieties farmers can rely on through good seasons and bad.
plos-pone-0354482: Nesprin1 — a nuclear envelope protein — may play an unexpected role in heart failure. This paper explored its role in isoproterenol-induced heart failure, probing pathogenesis and therapeutic implications. The findings nominate a novel molecular player in the heart’s decline — and potential rescue.
plos-pone-0347282: Artificial sweeteners’ effects on bones and joints were poorly understood. This report examined sweetener mechanisms in four musculoskeletal disorders using network toxicology, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics. The computational toxicology reveals unexpected molecular interactions — with implications for millions of daily sweetener users.
plos-pone-0355482: Counting carbon in plantation forests requires equations tuned to each species and site. This paper improved carbon stock estimates with site-specific allometric equations for Gmelina arborea in Ghana’s Kwahu Highlands. The tailored equations make carbon credits — and climate claims — more honest.
europmc-pmc2837382: Ecologists trace diets with stable isotopes, but messy data can mislead. This 2010 paper offers statistical tools for source partitioning when variation is high. The authors show how to cope with too much noise in isotope mixing models. Their methods made diet reconstruction more honest about uncertainty.
europmc-pmc2852382: Bowel surgery can go wrong in set ways, and this 2010 review names them. The authors list risk factors for snags in colon and rectum surgery and how to head them off. Their checklist aids safer operations. The review serves wards that want fewer returns to the operating room.
europmc-pmc2876182: White blood cells spit out toxic granules to kill germs, and this 2006 paper explains the machinery. The author details the mechanisms of degranulation in neutrophils. Their overview covers the trigger and release. The review remains a primer on a front-line immune weapon.
europmc-pmc2908682: To learn what tiny RNAs do in plants, researchers built decoys. This 2010 paper offers a collection of target mimics for studying microRNA function in Arabidopsis thaliana. The authors' toolkit lets scientists block each microRNA. Their resource opened systematic probing of plant microRNAs.
europmc-pmc3022582: Gene silencing locks onto the first exon. This 2011 paper shows methylation of a gene's first exon tracks gene shutdown closely. The authors reveal the lock's placement. Their work refined epigenetic rules. Promoter marks proved less telling, they find. Drug hunters now aim at the first exon.
europmc-pmc3072482: Migraine and mental illness travel together. This 2011 review surveys the overlap of migraine with anxiety and depression. The authors map the shared burden. Their overview guides joint treatment. Treating one often eases the other. Doctors now screen migraineurs for mood.
europmc-pmc3084482: Tobacco smoke hides thousands of hazards. This 2011 review catalogs the poisons riding each puff of tobacco smoke. The authors' list runs into the thousands. Their overview informs regulation. Seventy of them are known carcinogens. Regulators use the list to set limits.
europmc-pmc3085482: A plant sensor juggles growth, death, and defense. This 2011 paper shows the BAK1 protein balances growth, cell suicide, and germ defense. The authors reveal the juggling act. Their work lights up plant signaling. One switch steers three fates. Crops may borrow the balancing trick.
europmc-pmc3095282: Wheat's tiny RNAs answer mildew and heat. This 2010 paper finds wheat microRNAs that switch on against mildew and heat. The authors reveal the responders. Their work aids crop breeding. Tough strains flip more switches. Breeders select for the busy responders.
europmc-pmc3096582: Behavior change got a wheel. This 2011 paper brings a wheel-shaped guide for designing behavior-change programs. The authors' framework spread through public health. Their work shaped campaigns. Smoking-cessation teams use it daily. The wheel links causes to tactics. It is now taught in health schools.
europmc-pmc6571782: Olive oil's health halo may come down to hydroxytyrosol and tyrosol - phenolic compounds abundant in the oil. This review gathers what is known about the pair and their chemical cousins: antioxidant and anti-inflammatory effects in lab and animal studies. The evidence backs the Mediterranean diet's star ingredient, with human trials still catching up.
europmc-pmc6597582: Genome studies keep tripping over the same bad neighborhoods - regions where sequencing signals pile up for technical, not biological, reasons. The ENCODE blacklist catalogs these problematic stretches across human, mouse, worm, and fly genomes. Filtering them out cleans up results and stops phantom findings before they start.
europmc-pmc6625982: When cells cannot run autophagy - their recycling program - odd LC3-decorated structures pile up instead. This study characterizes these LC3-positive blobs in autophagy-deficient cells, tracing where the stalled machinery jams. The findings illuminate what happens when the cell's cleanup crew goes on strike.
europmc-pmc6636482: Artery-clogging starts early - with oxidized cholesterol and smoldering inflammation. This review argues for striking at early atherosclerosis by calming oxidative stress and inflammation together. The strategy targets the disease's roots rather than its late wreckage, a prevention-minded take on heart disease.
europmc-pmc6761482: Most plants partner with underground fungi - arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi that trade nutrients for sugars. This review covers their role in growth and stress tolerance: how the fungal allies help crops weather drought, salt, and poor soils. The ancient symbiosis is modern agriculture's helper.
europmc-pmc6763482: The blood-brain barrier keeps drugs out of the brain - a problem for ALS therapy. In a first-in-human trial, focused ultrasound briefly opened the barrier in ALS patients, letting medicines through. The MR-guided technique proved safe and feasible - a door cracked open for future treatments.
europmc-pmc6770382: Pancreatic cancer shrugs off chemotherapy that works elsewhere - and patients pay the price. This review dissects chemoresistance in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma: the pumps, shields, and stroma that blunt drugs. Each defense mapped is a crack future therapies can widen.
gao-gaoreports-b-309982: A Government Accountability Office bid-protest decision dated October 25, 2007, filed by the Pacific Lock Company. The lock manufacturer challenged a federal contract award, and the ruling applies procurement law to its claims. Published decisions like this one preserve the reasoning GAO uses to judge competitions — guidance for every company bidding on government padlocks, hardware, and beyond.
gao-gaoreports-b-299382: C. Martin Company took its April 2007 contract fight to GAO, and this ruling is the call. The firm challenged the award; the ruling tests the claims against bid law. Family-named firms get the same formal hearing as the corporate giants.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-82: The YouthBuild program needed proof in 2007, and GAO's report says analyzing outcome data was the only way to judge its long-term benefits. The findings demand the evidence. The report asks whether the second chances were really changing lives. The program had to prove its worth.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-282: Locking down the world's loose radioactive material needed focus in 2007, and GAO's report says the Energy Department's threat-reduction program should aim its future efforts better. The findings set the priorities. The report argues for guarding the worst stuff first. The glow could not wait.
openalex-w7204620182: In Brazil, patients often sue the state to get medicines the public health system does not provide. This article reviews the research on that trend: how court orders protect the right to health, and how they strain public budgets and planning. The authors weigh rights against management reality. A clear-eyed look at what happens when the courtroom becomes the pharmacy.
openalex-w7164811582: Ising machines make mistakes, and this paper asks how best to fix them. The authors reframe error mitigation as a design problem, comparing two architectures, penalty-spin versus other replica-coupled models, using simulated annealing as a clean testbed. They judge the structures head to head. A systems-level study of making novel computers reliable.
openalex-w4416781482: Batteries live or die by how ions hop inside them, and muons can watch the hopping. This paper simulates muon spin signals in battery materials, modeling ion jumps with an extended relaxation function. The authors connect the math to real diffusion data. A methods study giving battery researchers a sharper lens on ion motion.
openalex-w7160514682: Malaria still kills, and new drugs are needed. This paper reports actinomycin derivatives isolated from a Streptomyces library with stronger selectivity against malaria parasites. The authors scaled up the search from a promising pilot screen. A natural-products study of soil microbes versus a global killer.
pmc-13438882: This 2026 study measured hypertension control rates before and after a multicomponent quality improvement program in Medicare beneficiaries, primarily Hispanic patients. Structured programs — combining education, monitoring, and care coordination — moved the numbers. The result is a practical model for closing blood pressure gaps.
pmc-13544382: This 2026 vascular paper reports the safety of iliac vein stenting performed in office-based labs, drawing on experience with 4,312 nonthrombotic lesions. Moving the procedure out of hospitals cuts costs, but safety must be proven. The large series provides that evidence.
pmc-13428482: A 2026 systematic review and meta-analysis asking whether acceptance- and mindfulness-based interventions improve psychological flexibility in people with chronic pain. Flexibility — the ability to act on values despite pain — is a core treatment target. The pooled evidence tests whether these therapies deliver it.
pmc-13313082: A 2026 comment on a paper evaluating inflammation-associated blood indices for predicting malignancy in thyroid nodules. Scientific comments debate or refine published claims. The exchange sharpens the question of which blood markers actually predict thyroid cancer.
pmc-13575682: This 2026 perspective envisioned the next steps for machine learning models in integrated cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic care. The CKM framework needs predictive tools. The paper sketches the roadmap.
pmc-13469082: In this 2026 transplant paper, PIRCHE scores reclassified immunologic risk in patients with medium eplet mismatch. The epitope-based scoring refines donor matching. The clinical application is the step forward.
pmc-13420282: This 2026 case report described a suicide attempt by dual ethylene glycol (antifreeze) and rat poison ingestion. The combined poisoning posed complex toxicology. The case details the rescue.
pmc-13503882: This 2026 review by Tang and Kang covered ferroptotic propagation — from single-cell execution to tissue-scale death programs. Iron-driven death spreads between cells. The review synthesizes the propagation biology.
pmc-13448282: This 2026 conference abstract (BSLD-09) explored CXCL12's role in T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia infiltration of the central nervous system. The chemokine guided the leukemia's brain invasion. The abstract presents the exploration.
pmc-13529182: In this 2026 rheumatology paper, the geriatric nutritional risk index was associated with mortality in rheumatoid arthritis patients. Nutrition predicted survival. The index is a simple risk tool.
pmc-13499082: A 2026 food engineering paper on ohmic heating application in pork burger processing. The electrical heating cooked efficiently. The application is the innovation.
pmc-13501882: In this 2026 polymer physics paper, conformation-determined segmental dynamics in polylysine hydrobromide were studied — the impact of thermally induced beta-sheet formation on the glass transition (the title is truncated). The protein-like polymer's dynamics were probed. The conformation link is the insight.
pmc-13468582: This 2026 intervention study compared DHA alone, EPA+DHA, EPA+DHA+GLA, and EPA+DHA with or without vitamin D during chemotherapy in women with breast cancer (the title is truncated). The omega-3 regimens were head-to-head. The comparison is the evidence.
pmc-13451782: This 2026 pilot RCT tested a psycho-behavioral intervention's effects on cancer-related fatigue in colorectal cancer patients. The mind-body intervention was trialed. The pilot is the preliminary evidence.
pmc-13456882: A 2026 systematic review and mapping of behavior change interventions to reduce opioids in chronic non-cancer pain in primary care (the title is truncated). The behavior change techniques were mapped. The review guides deprescribing.
pmc-13429282: This 2026 study examined prenatal modafinil exposure and risk of major congenital anomalies and other adverse neonatal and pediatric outcomes. The wakefulness drug's pregnancy safety was tested. The risk data guide prescribing.
pmc-13592482: A 2026 epilepsy paper dissecting components of generalized onset seizures with focal evolution progressing to bilateral tonic-clonic seizures using quantitative EEG. The seizure's evolution was quantified. The components are the insight.
pmc-13450482: This 2026 materials paper achieved surfactantless electrophoretic deposition of nonaqueous CuO nanoparticle dispersions by tailoring surface defectiveness. The coating worked without surfactants. The tailoring is the trick.
pmc-13342482: A 2026 liver cancer paper: catecholamines activated a tumor progression program in differentiated tumor hepatocytes. The stress hormones drove the cancer. The activation is the mechanism.
pmc-13431882: A 2026 Drosophila paper: analysis of a hypomorphic mei-P26 mutation revealed coordination between developmental programming of germ cells and meiotic chromosome dynamics. The germline's coordination was decoded. The revealing is the developmental insight.
pmc-13511882: This 2026 review covered RNA splicing dysregulation in Parkinson's disease. The mis-spliced transcripts were surveyed. The review is the state of the field.
pmc-13452282: A 2026 case report of steerable microcatheter-assisted selective inflow embolization of a giant femoral artery bifurcation pseudoaneurysm. The tricky aneurysm was embolized. The case details the technique.
pmc-13434382: This 2026 case report described a huge intraosseous hemangioma in the maxillary sinus misdiagnosed as osteosarcoma. The benign tumor mimicked cancer. The case warns pathologists.
pmc-13435982: A 2026 trial protocol testing neuromuscular feedback therapy in chronic spinal cord injury patients with residual lower extremity motor function versus conventional therapy (the title is truncated). The protocol is the plan. The testing will compare the approaches.
pmc-13515882: In this 2026 paper, a magnetic milligripper platform was presented for biomedical and biological applications. The tiny magnetic gripper manipulated cells. The platform is the microrobotics advance.
pmc-13453482: A 2026 systematic review and meta-analysis of immune checkpoint inhibitors' impact on infection in solid malignancy patients (the title is truncated). The immunotherapy-infection risk was pooled. The review guides oncology.
pmc-13427082: This 2026 paper examined chikungunya vaccine approval in Brazil — navigating epidemiological challenges and immunization strategies. The vaccine's rollout context was analyzed. The navigating informs policy.
pmc-13427982: A 2026 case report: successful destination therapy after stepwise mechanical circulatory support in cardiogenic shock following mechanical aortic valve replacement (the title is truncated). The staged support saved the patient. The case is the feat.
pmc-13417482: This 2026 correction notice amended an initial report on differential expression of Sprouty proteins 1 and 2 in human epithelial ovarian cancer cell lines. Corrections fix the record. This entry preserves the correction.
arxiv-2606-16682: AI agents that improve themselves need evaluators to judge their progress — but multimodal evaluators can suffer "preference collapse," where coupled modalities distort the judgment. This paper documents that cross-modal coupling in self-evolving agents. It targets researchers building agents that reliably get better on their own.
arxiv-2606-16782: Sunspots have a dark core (umbra) and a lighter fringe (penumbra). This paper studies those features on V1298 Tau — a young, Sun-like star — using JWST data, as part of the KRONOS II program. It is for stellar astronomers studying how young stars' spots differ from our Sun's.
